To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the insertion of the biogenesis factor Rei1 into the ribosomal exit tunnel is a key event in the final steps of 60 S ribosome assembly.

the insertion of the ribosome biogenesis factor Rei1 into the 60S ribosome polypeptide exit channel is required for the release of other biogenesis factors, and that the insertion of Rei1 into the tunnel is facilitated by a network of interactions between Rei1 and Alb1.
the insertion of the ribosome biogenesis factor Rei1 in the exit tunnel of the ribosome is essential to complete the maturation of the 60S subunits.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure and function of the ribosomal exit tunnel.
the structure and mechanism of action of a ribosome biogenesis factor complex.
the molecular mechanisms of eukaryotic ribosomal biogenesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the C terminus insertion of Rei1 is a critical step for 60S maturing, and the Rei1 C terminus insertion into the ribosomal exit tunnel is a quality control mechanism for the ribosome biogenesis.

the structure of the yeast ribosome with the biogenesis factor Rei1, ArX1, and Alb-1 at 3,4 A resolution reveals the mechanism of the integrity of the exit tunnel and the insertion of Rei-1 in the tunnel.
Rei1 and Arx1 are essential for the proofreading of the 60S subunits.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Rei1 probes the integrity of the exit tunnel and that its insertion is required for 60S maturing.
insertion of the biogenesis factor Rei1 probes the ribosomal tunnel during 60S matuation.
the insertion of the C terminus into the ribosomal exit tunnel is required to release Rei1 from the ribosome.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ribosomal polynucleotide exit tunnel is a site for the action of biogenesis factors during the maturation of 60S ribosome subunits.
Rei1, a biogenesis factor that is conserved in eukaryotes, probes the exit tunnel of the large subunit to monitor the integrity of the 60S subunits during the final steps of 60 S biogenesis.
Rei1 and Arx1 act as quality-control factors to ensure the integrity of the 60S subunits.
